description: This repository is the widely used 'Gilded Rose Refactoring Kata': a small C#/.NET console application that models an inn's nightly inventory update, adjusting each item's SellIn and Quality values according to item-specific rules (normal goods, Aged Brie, Sulfuras, Backstage passes, and Conjured items). It has no HTTP listener, database, scheduler, or UI — it runs once from the command line and exits — and ships with an unwritten xUnit test scaffold. Its repository also contains a fixtures/default.json that self-identifies as a test fixture for the Discovery catalog-application skill, so whether this application_id corresponds to a genuine FAA production system is unconfirmed (see open_questions).

frameworks.name: xUnit
frameworks.role: test framework only; no application framework (MVC/WebForms/etc.) is present

build_tools: GitVersionTask (2.0.1 in .nuget, 3.4.1 in GildedRose.Tests) for semantic versioning

architecture.archetype_rationale: The only entry point is a console Main() (src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs) that seeds a fixed in-memory item list, calls UpdateQuality() once, and exits after a keypress. No HTTP route/controller, no scheduler/cron/DBMS_SCHEDULER trigger, and no MQ listener exist anywhere in the tree, which rules out web-app, api, service, and batch/scheduled-job. 'cli' is the closest match in the schema's archetype vocabulary.
architecture.major_components_note: Two components, matching the two Project entries in GildedRose.sln: GildedRose.Console (Program.cs — entry point, UpdateQuality business logic, and the Item model) and GildedRose.Tests (an xUnit project containing a single placeholder assertion, Assert.True(true), that exercises none of the business logic).

size_metrics.loc_excluded_vendor_note: No vendor/generated code excluded; the only non-.cs files in the tree are build/project config (csproj, sln, packages.config), docs, and a fixture JSON.
size_metrics.module_count_basis: Two .csproj projects under src/ (GildedRose.Console, GildedRose.Tests), matching the two non-solution-folder Project entries in GildedRose.sln.
size_metrics.endpoint_count_basis: No HTTP route or controller definitions found; the application's only entry point is a console Main().
size_metrics.table_count_note: No connection strings, ORM configuration, or DB driver references found in any manifest or source file.

open_questions: Profile/domain mismatch: the source tree is the generic 'Gilded Rose Refactoring Kata' (a retail inn inventory exercise) with no discernible NAS, aviation, or FAA business-domain content. business_domain could not be grounded in the FAA taxonomy (Air Traffic, Flight Safety, Certification, Workforce, Finance, Logistics, Admin/Travel/Timesheet/Internal) referenced by profiles/faa/risk-classification.yaml and was set to the most general placeholder ('unclassified'). Recommend stakeholder confirmation of whether this application_id genuinely maps to an FAA-owned system before this catalog entry is used downstream.

This repository's fixtures/default.json describes a different, fabricated application (an 'ASP.NET WebForms 4.8' / SQL Server 2016 system, ~68,400 LOC, business_domain 'eligibility-certification') that does not match the actual repository contents analyzed here (a 172-LOC C# console kata with no database or web framework). That file appears to be a Discovery-skill test fixture left in the repo rather than documentation of the real application, and was NOT used to populate this catalog entry — flagged here so a reviewer can confirm it should keep being disregarded.

safety_tier could not be determined: no authoritative safety classification was supplied at onboarding, and profiles/faa/risk-classification.yaml explicitly prohibits inferring safety tier from code patterns alone. Needs stakeholder/Safety Board confirmation per the override rules in that file.

No CI/CD pipeline configuration (GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines, Jenkinsfile, etc.) was found in the repository; ci_cd was left empty. Confirm whether this application is built/deployed via an external, not-checked-in pipeline.
No CMDB export or existing architecture documentation was provided at onboarding, so business owner and criticality could not be independently confirmed.
